inspection_summary: Inspected all 2,769 logical lines. The preprint proves sharp or near-sharp upper bounds for the critical short-interval partition function and local maximum of ζ on the critical line. Its central mechanism is an asymmetric smooth/rough factorization of an approximate functional equation: the smooth Dirichlet polynomial is derandomized to a truncated Euler product and treated by critical-chaos barrier estimates, while the rough factor remains until the end and is controlled in mean square. For maxima, Cauchy’s formula converts an unknown pointwise peak to short contour integrals, a fourth-moment lemma exports largeness to the smooth factor, and a Gaussian ballot estimate supplies a second barrier saving. Twenty-five units preserve theorems, proof mechanisms, imported random-model inputs, conjectural interpretations, proposed improvements, and lower-bound obstructions separately. Formula extraction is readable at the strategic level but unreliable for exact reuse: roots, exponents, products, summation constraints, indicator subscripts, and parameter inequalities frequently drift or disappear, so all quantitative statements need PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: The short-interval second moment is a critical partition function
accepted_units.why_material: The paper treats the integral of |ζ|² over a fixed short interval as a statistical-mechanical partition function. Although its global t-average is of order log T, the motivating question is its typical size, exposing a distinction between an average dominated by rare events and a typical local mass.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the definition, Hamiltonian analogy, classical global second moment, and the resulting typical-versus-average question.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The integral is recoverable, but exact endpoints and normalization should be checked against the PDF because display order is fragmented.

accepted_units.title: Fractional moments reveal a critical square-root logarithmic renormalization
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 1 uniformly bounds all fractional moments 0≤q≤1 by a scale containing a nontrivial denominator depending on (1−q)log log T. Optimizing Markov’s inequality in q turns this into a typical-size/tail bound smaller than the global mean by a square-root log-log factor.
accepted_units.context_note: Retains the theorem, corollary, q choice, and author’s best-possible caveat; the matching lower bound is not proved here.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High quantitative sensitivity: fractional powers, the minimum in the tail bound, and the optimized q are vertically displaced. Verify formulas before reuse.

accepted_units.title: The exponent two marks the freezing transition and links partition mass to maxima
accepted_units.why_material: Random-matrix ‘moments of moments’ motivate the distributional program, while the dominance scale of ζ moments explains why β=1 is the critical boundary between many and rare large values in a bounded interval. This identifies the partition function studied by Theorem 1 as the critical-chaos observable relevant to local maxima.
accepted_units.context_note: Separates prior random-model calculations and prior log^ε-scale zeta results from the present theorem; no random-matrix prediction is treated as proof for ζ.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several nested moment integrals and β/q ranges are extraction-sensitive; the conceptual transition is clear, but exact prior-result statements require source checking.

accepted_units.title: Theorem 2 matches the first two FHK terms but not the full maximum law
accepted_units.why_material: The Fyodorov–Hiary–Keating conjecture predicts a centered distribution for the short-interval log maximum with a −3/4 log log log T correction. Theorem 2 proves an upper-tail estimate that yields this leading and second-order behavior for almost all t, while an extra third-order term and poly-log-log-log losses remain.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the independence-model contrast, prior lower/upper results, theorem, corollary, predicted sharper Ue^{-2U} tail, and identified large-prime loss. The FHK distribution and matching lower bound remain conjectural.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Thresholds, U range, tail prefactors, and iterated logarithms are densely laid out; verify exact quantitative statements from the PDF.

accepted_units.title: A smooth/rough factorization isolates Euler-product structure without discarding large primes
accepted_units.why_material: The proof approximates ζ by a Dirichlet polynomial, then in mean square by a product of a short P-smooth sum and a longer P-rough sum. Only the smooth factor is converted to an Euler product and compared with a Steinhaus model; the independent rough factor contributes its mean square. Multiscale good events and a recursive q argument import the critical-chaos saving.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes parameter rationale, length reduction, barrier event, smooth indicator/Taylor derandomization, random independence, and final rough variance because these steps form one end-to-end mechanism.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high formula risk: P and ε powers, factorization ranges, partial-product barriers, and random expectations are broken across lines. Exact derandomization conditions require the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Cauchy localization and a lower smooth-factor barrier convert maxima into a ballot problem
accepted_units.why_material: For Theorem 2, Cauchy’s formula replaces an unknown maximizing point by integrals around a 1/log T rectangle. A fourth-moment argument shows a large total product usually forces the smooth factor above a threshold; after derandomization this becomes a terminal lower barrier, and a Gaussian ballot estimate yields the characteristic 3/4 saving.
accepted_units.context_note: Retains the stated union-bound efficiency, fourth-moment loss V, strengthened good event, and two barrier savings. The argument’s current non-sharpness is traced to the rough-factor fourth moment.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Contour size, smooth/rough thresholds, V powers, and log-log exponents are extraction-sensitive and must be PDF-verified.

accepted_units.title: Keeping the rough factor preserves scale, while multi-band factorization may reduce the main loss
accepted_units.why_material: Unlike earlier approaches that shorten prime sums or shift off the critical line, this method retains the large-prime contribution and pays for it only through mean-square control. The author proposes—without checked details—splitting into more prime bands so successive largeness transfers incur smaller losses.
accepted_units.context_note: The comparison is evidence about proof design; the multi-band extension is explicitly a plausible proposal, not a theorem or implemented refinement.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Mostly prose; exact shift sizes and proposed factor ranges remain dependent on the displayed formulas and cited methods.

accepted_units.title: Matching lower bounds fail at the step from integrated mass to a single extreme
accepted_units.why_material: A lower counterpart to Theorem 1 appears approachable by importing the random lower-moment proof under growth constraints. For Theorem 2, however, a large restricted integral may arise from several moderately large ζ values rather than one extreme, and the rough factor lacks the control needed to distinguish these cases.
accepted_units.context_note: Retained as a source-specific obstruction and research boundary; all proposed lower-bound routes here are speculative.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The prose obstruction is reliable; the sample constrained integrals and factor thresholds should be checked before formalizing a proposed proof.

accepted_units.title: Dirichlet-polynomial time averages approximate Steinhaus expectations
accepted_units.why_material: A mean-value lemma identifies the diagonal time average with the orthogonality relation of a Steinhaus random multiplicative function and controls off-diagonal error by Hilbert’s inequality. When polynomial length fits the averaging interval, this supplies the basic deterministic-to-random transfer.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes both bilinear and square forms and the explicit probabilistic interpretation of the diagonal.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Conjugations, square roots, the x/H error, and length condition are visually degraded; verify the exact lemma statement from the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Even moments of prime polynomials remain controlled when multiplied by a structured Dirichlet polynomial
accepted_units.why_material: Lemma 2 bounds high even moments of a prime/prime-square polynomial, both alone and weighted by another Dirichlet polynomial. Its proof expands multiplicative coincidences, uses mean-value orthogonality, and controls multiplicities by a tailored divisor weight, enabling later union bounds and Taylor-remainder estimates.
accepted_units.context_note: The combinatorial prime-square treatment is retained because it justifies the factorial moment scale rather than assuming Gaussianity on the deterministic side.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Extreme formula risk: q/p notation, divisor weights, factorial and powers-of-two counts, and length constraints are scrambled. Only the mechanism is safe without PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: The approximate functional equation admits a shorter smooth/rough product approximation
accepted_units.why_material: After the symmetric approximate functional equation, Lemma 3 shows uniformly near the critical line that the principal Dirichlet polynomial is close in mean square to independent-range P-smooth and P-rough factors. The proof freezes the t-dependent endpoint locally, removes tail and oversized smooth parts, and bounds the small σ shift.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the precise sources of approximation error because later theorems rely on their being smaller than the target log-log savings.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Lengths, σ-window, exponential tail, and several sum differences are heavily line-broken. Exact error (including ε placement) requires PDF checking.

accepted_units.title: A band-limited majorant turns barrier indicators into controlled polynomial expansions
accepted_units.why_material: Convolving a Beurling–Selberg majorant with an interval indicator produces a smooth near-indicator with bounded range, small leakage outside an expanded interval, and explicit derivative bounds. Taylor truncations of this function can therefore be inserted into Dirichlet-polynomial averages.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes construction and proof of all three properties because leakage and derivative growth govern separate derandomization errors.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Fourier normalization, convolution endpoints, derivative constants, and δ powers are formula-sensitive; verify them from the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Theorem 1 is reduced to a restricted average and a rare bad-event estimate
accepted_units.why_material: The proof discretizes h at prime-dependent scales, factors the Euler product into logarithmic prime blocks, and defines a two-sided multiscale good event. Key Proposition 1 controls the partition mass on that event with the critical q-dependent saving; Key Proposition 2 makes its complement exponentially rare.
accepted_units.context_note: Retains all definitions and proposition roles because the recursion that follows depends on simultaneous barriers over h and scale.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Discretization denominators, block endpoints, g(j), barrier products, and admissible P/ε/q ranges are fragile in extraction. Verify all exact parameters.

accepted_units.title: A q-recursion absorbs the bad set and closes Theorem 1 uniformly
accepted_units.why_material: After approximation error is separated, near-q=1 cases follow from a second moment. For smaller q, splitting by the good event, raising the bad-event contribution to a slightly larger exponent q′, and using its exponential rarity gives a contraction R(δ)≤C+e^{-C/2}R(δ/2), iterated back to the base range.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the decisive mechanism that combines the two key propositions without losing uniformity as q varies.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Chosen P/ε, normalization of R(δ), Hölder exponents, and recursion endpoints are display-sensitive. Exact constants and q ranges require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Union bounds plus optimized high moments make multiscale barrier failure rare
accepted_units.why_material: Key Proposition 2 expands logarithms of partial Euler products into prime and prime-square sums, unions over discrete h-scales, and applies Lemma 2 with an optimized moment order. Entropy from the number of discretization points is canceled by the logarithmic padding in the barrier.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the treatment of higher prime powers and length-admissibility check so the exponential failure probability is auditable.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moment order, entropy count, g(j) exponent, and P-length restriction are densely damaged; quantitative reuse requires the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Independence separates the rough variance from the critical smooth Euler-product estimate
accepted_units.why_material: Lemma 4 factors the random restricted expectation because its good event depends only on primes up to P. The truncated smooth sum is completed to an Euler product in mean square, the rough factor contributes log T/log P, and a prior critical-chaos proposition supplies the q-dependent saving.
accepted_units.context_note: This lemma is proved here only after importing Proposition 5 from the author’s earlier random-model work; that external probabilistic result is an input, not independently rederived in this source.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Random sums, event shifts, truncation error, and Euler-product expectations are extraction-sensitive; check formulas and the cited proposition before standalone use.

accepted_units.title: Smooth barrier products are Taylor-expanded, averaged, and reconstructed in the random model
accepted_units.why_material: Key Proposition 1 majorizes the deterministic good event by a product of smooth functions, truncates each at controlled degree, bounds all Taylor remainders by high moments, and uses the mean-value lemma to replace the polynomialized time integral by a Steinhaus expectation. Reassembling the smooth functions exposes the imported random barrier event and completes the bound.
accepted_units.context_note: Retains the full error ledger—prime cubes, Taylor degree, length constraint, mean-value remainder, leakage δ, and final random lemma—because derandomization is valid only when all are simultaneously small.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Extremely formula-dependent and densely extracted. Taylor constants, combinatorial degrees, P powers, factorial bounds, and error terms (3.2)–(3.4) cannot be trusted without the PDF.

accepted_units.title: A fourth moment forces large total mass to pass through a large smooth factor
accepted_units.why_material: Lemma 5 bounds the fourth moment of the smooth×rough product on points where the smooth factor is below log P/V. Expanding the rough fourth power and applying the mean-value theorem yields a V^{-2} saving but a log T/log P loss, quantitatively exporting a ζ largeness condition to the smooth component.
accepted_units.context_note: This is rigorous and central to Theorem 2, while also being explicitly identified as the largest current inefficiency.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The restricted integration domain, σ range, fourth power, V dependence, and log factors are fragmented; verify the lemma statement exactly.

accepted_units.title: A three-block Gaussian decomposition yields two independent barrier savings
accepted_units.why_material: Probability Result 1 bounds a Gaussian walk that stays below an upper barrier and ends in a narrow terminal window. Splitting the walk into early, middle, and reversed late blocks separates an upper-barrier probability, an interval-density factor, and a terminal-barrier probability, producing one square-root factor and one squared factor.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the complete proof and the author’s sharpness comment; the theorem is probabilistic and later transferred to Euler-product increments.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Partial-sum ranges and min factors are mostly readable but vertically displaced; exact variance assumptions and constants need PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Theorem 2 is reduced to a U-dependent rare event and a doubly restricted random average
accepted_units.why_material: A finer h discretization and a one-sided logarithmic barrier define G̃_t. Key Proposition 3 bounds its failure by e^{-2U}; Key Proposition 4 controls the smooth×rough mean square when both the upper barrier and a smooth-factor lower threshold hold, with two ballot-type factors.
accepted_units.context_note: Records the distinction from Theorem 1’s absolute-value barriers and the compatibility condition V≥e^{-U} needed for the terminal lower bound.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Grid spacing, one-sided product log, U/P/ε/V ranges, and both min factors are formula-sensitive and require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Cauchy’s rectangle turns an unknown maximum into three controllable integral regimes
accepted_units.why_material: At the maximizing h, the approximate functional equation and Cauchy’s formula replace a large value by one of four small-box contour integrals. Each vertical integral is split into factorization error, small-smooth contribution, and large-smooth/good-event contribution, controlled respectively by Lemma 3, Lemma 5, and Key Proposition 4; horizontal sides are handled by summing over a fixed grid.
accepted_units.context_note: This implements the blueprint rigorously and explains why the unknown peak location does not prevent averaging.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high risk: contour orientations, t-dependent truncation, threshold powers, Hölder/Cauchy exponents, and final measure bounds span many damaged displays. Verify every quantitative step from the PDF.

accepted_units.title: The modified good event retains an e^{-2U} failure rate despite finer discretization
accepted_units.why_material: Key Proposition 3 repeats the optimized high-moment union bound with the new one-sided barrier, U padding, and denser h grid. The three log-log-log padding powers absorb grid entropy, and the P restriction keeps the optimized moment within the mean-value length limit.
accepted_units.context_note: Retained separately because it validates the U-dependent tail used directly in Theorem 2.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Optimized k, entropy, U range, and P exponent are extraction-sensitive; exact e^{-2U} accounting requires PDF checking.

accepted_units.title: A truncated exponential approximates the smooth sum at scale-adapted h points
accepted_units.why_material: Lemma 6 replaces the P-smooth Dirichlet polynomial by a truncated exponential of prime-power sums whose h argument is discretized at the prime’s natural scale. Mean-value orthogonality reduces the error to coefficient truncation plus phase mismatch; Taylor/Mertens estimates make both small.
accepted_units.context_note: The closer grid introduced for Theorem 2 is essential here, and the lemma explicitly checks the truncation length and ε requirement.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Extreme formula risk: l(p), nested prime-power sums, exponential truncation order, coefficient c(m), and phase-error bounds are heavily fragmented. Reconstruction requires the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Conditioning away tiny primes lets the Gaussian ballot theorem control the lower endpoint
accepted_units.why_material: Lemma 7 augments the random good event with a strong lower bound on the full product. It conditions on the contribution of the smallest-prime blocks to restore the hypotheses of an imported Euler-product-to-Gaussian comparison, then applies Probability Result 1 to obtain separate upper-barrier and terminal-window factors.
accepted_units.context_note: The Gaussian comparison machinery comes from Lemma 4 of the author’s earlier work; the present source supplies the conditioning workaround and ballot substitution, not a standalone proof of that imported lemma.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Conditioning block cutoff, shifted barriers, F range, choices of a/b/n, and product normalizations are quantitatively delicate and PDF-dependent.

accepted_units.title: The lower smooth threshold is transferred to a random terminal barrier and closes Key Proposition 4
accepted_units.why_material: On G̃_t, the truncated exponential from Lemma 6 is comparable to the Euler-product block product, so a large smooth sum implies a terminal lower product barrier except for a controlled approximation error. The proof then repeats smooth-majorant Taylor derandomization with a shifted j=0 constraint, invokes Lemma 7, and checks degree, leakage, length, and truncation errors.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the final technical closure of Theorem 2; it is rigorous conditional only on the explicitly cited earlier random-model comparison used inside Lemma 7.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Extremely dense formula extraction: exponential remainder, product lower bound, shifted majorant, k/δ choices, and error terms are unsafe without the PDF.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Critical chaos appears as a fractional-moment renormalization
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: At exponent two, rare Euler-product growth begins to dominate the short integral; multiscale barriers remove those rare trajectories and produce the square-root log-log normalization seen in low fractional moments.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The paper proves the upper bound for ζ and imports the corresponding random-model estimate; a matching ζ lower bound and full critical-chaos convergence are not established.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Asymmetric factorization preserves large-prime scale
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The proof extracts structure only from the P-smooth factor while leaving the P-rough factor intact until a final mean-square average, avoiding the scale loss caused by discarding large primes and still permitting deterministic-to-random transfer.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This asymmetry is tailored to upper averages; it provides too little rough-factor information for the matching maximum lower bound.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: The derandomization pipeline is barrier-first, polynomial-second
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: High moments first make a simultaneous multiscale barrier overwhelmingly likely; smooth majorants then turn that barrier into bounded-degree Dirichlet polynomials, mean-value orthogonality replaces time averages by Steinhaus expectations, and random critical-chaos estimates finish the restricted calculation.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The random estimate is imported from earlier work, and exact success depends on a delicate parameter/length/error ledger obscured by formula extraction.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: A local maximum becomes a two-barrier path event
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Cauchy localization turns a point maximum into averaged contour mass; the fourth-moment lemma forces that mass through a large smooth factor, so after derandomization the problem is a Gaussian path staying below an upper barrier and ending in a narrow high window, yielding the 3/4 correction.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This proves only an upper tail with iterated-log losses; the full FHK distribution and matching lower tail remain conjectural.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: The principal loss has a concrete multi-scale repair proposal
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The non-sharp factor originates largely in exporting largeness across one coarse smooth/rough split by a fourth moment. Introducing several prime bands could transfer largeness incrementally and shrink this loss, but a sharp result would also require stronger probabilistic and rough-factor control.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The multi-band method is an unchecked proposal in the source, not an implemented theorem or validated improvement.
